eyebrow: System of action vs. system of record
code:
ServiceNow:                    Other platforms:
- system of action              - Workday / SuccessFactors: employee data
- runs & tracks the process     - monitoring tools: infrastructure state
- approves, routes, closes      - Salesforce: customer data
                                 - legacy ticketing: pre-merger tickets
caption: ServiceNow rarely owns the data it needs to act on.

code:
Without integration:                With integration:
HR hires someone in Workday         Workday pushes the hire
  -> human notices, re-types          -> ServiceNow onboarding
  -> hours/days of delay                 starts automatically
  -> typos, drift                     -> correct data, no lag
caption: Every manual re-entry point is a delay and a drift risk.

steps.label: Receiving
steps.sub: a monitoring tool auto-creates an Incident the moment it detects an outage

steps.label: Initiating
steps.sub: an approved Change calls out to a deployment tool to carry out the work

code:
Trigger happens OUTSIDE ServiceNow?    Trigger happens INSIDE ServiceNow?
  -> build inbound                       -> build outbound

Choice is dictated by where the event fires,
not by whichever direction is easier to build.
caption: A real integration developer builds either direction.
